sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW OVER THE CONUS IN RECENT DAYS WILL AMPLIFY THIS PERIOD AS JET STREAKS NOW OVER AB...MT...AND WY SWEEP RAPIDLY SEWD...RESULTING IN A DEEP BUT PROGRESSIVE TROUGH OVER THE LWR OH VLY BY 12Z THU. IN THE MEANTIME...UPR IMPULSE THAT CROSSED E TX YESTERDAY WILL CONTINUE TO BECOME ABSORBED WITHIN STRONG AND FURTHER STRENGTHENING SW FLOW OVER THE SERN STATES. THE MAIN PART OF THAT DISTURBANCE IS OVER MS ATTM...AND SHOULD REACH PIEDMONT NC BY EARLY EVE AS A HIGH LVL JET ENTRANCE REGION DEVELOPS OVER THE MID ATLANTIC IN RESPONSE TO AMPLIFICATION OF LARGER SCALE TROUGH. AT THE SFC...SEASONABLY RICH MOISTURE /WITH SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S F AND PW AROUND 1.50 INCHES/...WILL CONTINUE TO STREAM NEWD ACROSS GA AND THE CAROLINAS TO VICINITY OF STNRY FRONT OVER VA. SFC WAVE NOW OVER NRN MS/AL SHOULD REDEVELOP ENE ALONG THE FRONT INTO CNTRL VA LATER TODAY. ADDITIONAL WEAK WAVES LIKELY WILL DEVELOP ALONG THE BOUNDARY UNTIL IT FINALLY CLEARS THE CAROLINA CST AS A COLD FRONT LATER THU MORNING.

sections.title: LWR MS VLY/ERN GULF CST INTO CAROLINAS/MID-ATLANTIC
sections.text: BAND OF SCTD SUPERCELLS ALONG LOW LVL CONFLUENCE AXIS OVER SE LA/ERN MS AND WRN AL LIKELY WILL PERSIST FOR AT LEAST A WHILE LONGER THIS MORNING AS THE AXIS EDGES SLOWLY EWD IN RESPONSE TO EJECTING UPR IMPULSE. COMBINATION OF RICH MOISTURE INFLOW AND STRONG LOW LVL SHEAR MAY CONTINUE TO FOSTER LOW LVL ROTATION/ISOLD TORNADOES AS THE FEATURES CROSSES AL /REF WWS 887 888/. WITH TIME...MODEST DIURNAL HEATING MAY FOSTER REJUVENATION OF THE CONFLUENCE AXIS STORMS. MORE LIKELY...HOWEVER...HEATING WILL SUPPORT EVENTUAL ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT EAST OF THE CONFLUENCE AXIS OVER PARTS OF GA AND THE CAROLINAS...S AND E OF SHALLOW RAIN-REINFORCED BOUNDARY ALONG THE SRN SLOPES OF THE APPALACHIANS. WEAKENING OF UPR IMPULSE IN CONFLUENT FLOW ALOFT SUGGESTS THAT LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE WEAK. BUT COMBINATION OF EVEN WEAK DESTABILIZATION /SBCAPE TO 1000 J PER KG/ WITH STRONG VEERING WIND PROFILES /40 KT SW 850 MB FLOW BENEATH 60-70 KT WSW FLOW AT 500 MB/ LIKELY WILL SUPPORT SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS. THESE MAY ORGANIZE INTO BROKEN BANDS THAT WILL POSE A RISK FOR BOTH TORNADOES AND NARROW SWATHS OF DMGG WIND...ESPECIALLY ACROSS APPALACHIAN FOOTHILLS/PIEDMONT OF GA AND THE CAROLINAS/VA.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: VORTICITY MAXIMUM OVER TN/MS/AL WILL LIFT NEWD THROUGH THE SRN APPALACHIANS TO OFF THE MID ATLANTIC COAST BY LATE TONIGHT IN ADVANCE OF A STRONGER UPSTREAM IMPULSE WHICH WILL AMPLIFY OVER THE MID/LOWER MS VALLEY DURING THE LATTER HALF OF THE D1 PERIOD. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE WAVE ANALYZED OVER N-CNTRL AL AS OF 15Z WILL DEVELOP RAPIDLY NEWD ALONG BAROCLINIC ZONE TO CNTRL VA BY 17/00Z. IN ITS WAKE...A TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE SEWD THROUGH THE CNTRL GULF COAST STATES...AND THE FOOTHILLS AND PIEDMONT OF THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS. ALONG THIS FRONT... SECONDARY CYCLOGENESIS IS FORECAST LATE TONIGHT INTO THU MORNING OVER NRN SC/SRN NC.

sections.title: CNTRL GULF COAST EWD THROUGH THE SERN AND MID ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: NNE-SSW BAND OF TSTMS /WITH EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS/ IS ONGOING ACROSS AL THIS MORNING WITH ACTIVITY LIKELY BEING FORCED BY VORTICITY MAXIMUM MENTIONED ABOVE. AMBIENT WARM SECTOR AIR MASS IS CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPE VALUES OF 250-500 J/KG OVER THE SRN APPALACHIANS AND 1000-1500 J/KG NEARER TO THE GULF COAST. LATEST MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT THE STRONGEST FORCING FOR ASCENT AND VERTICAL SHEAR WILL COINCIDE WITH MIGRATORY SURFACE LOW AND ALONG ATTENDANT SURFACE BAROCLINIC ZONE OVER NRN GA THIS AFTERNOON. FARTHER S/SW...SUFFICIENT MOISTURE AND INSTABILITY WILL PERSIST TO SUSTAIN ONGOING STORMS EWD ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF CNTRL/SRN AL INTO GA AND THE FL PNHDL TODAY INTO THIS EVENING. FOR ADDITIONAL NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE ON THIS AREA...SEE MCD 2331 AND TORNADO WATCH 889. ADDITIONAL CLUSTERS OF TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM IN THE LEE OF THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS BEFORE SPREADING EWD ACROSS THE PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. HERE TOO...WARM SECTOR ENVIRONMENT WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY A MOIST AND MARGINALLY TO MODERATELY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR WITH MLCAPE VALUES UP TO 1000-1500 J/KG. BOTH LOW AND DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL STEADILY STRENGTHEN THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE D1 PE

sections.title: 20Z OUTLOOK UPDATE
sections.text: ONE AREA OF STRONGER MID/UPPER FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION HAS LIFTED NORTH OF THE MID ATLANTIC COAST STATES...WITH ANOTHER AREA NOW DEVELOPING NORTH OF THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS. A COUPLE OF IMPULSES ARE EVIDENT DIGGING UPSTREAM...ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS...BUT NOT LIKELY TO SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACT THE SOUTHEAST STATES UNTIL LATER TONIGHT. SO SUPPORT FOR A SUBSTANTIVE FURTHER INCREASE IN ONGOING CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY IS UNCLEAR...ASIDE FROM POSSIBLE INTENSIFICATION ASSOCIATED WITH PEAK BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING AND INSTABILITY. THE PRE-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT ACROSS CENTRAL GEORGIA THROUGH THE CAROLINAS IS EXPECTED TO BE GENERALLY CHARACTERIZED BY WEAK TO MODEST CAPE AND 40-50 KT WEST SOUTHWESTERLY DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW AND SHEAR THROUGH MID TO LATE EVENING. DESPITE THE LACK OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT...THIS WILL BE CONDUCIVE TO THE CONTINUING POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WINDS...AS WELL AS ISOLATED SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING TORNADOES. A DIFFERENTIAL HEATING BOUNDARY ACROSS THE PIEDMONT...ALONG WHICH MODELS SUGGEST A 50 KT 850 MB JET CORE WILL TRACK LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING...SEEMS TO PROV
